rounds.fact: Engadget launched in 2004 and quickly became one of the most-read gadget blogs, known for live-blogging tech keynotes years before that became a standard practice across tech media.
Photobucket became the default way millions of MySpace users hosted images for their profiles, since MySpace itself didn't offer easy photo uploading in its early years.
Metacafe was a serious early rival to YouTube, at one point drawing tens of millions of monthly viewers by paying creators for popular videos.
Instagram launched iPhone-only in late 2010 and hit 25,000 users on day one. Its web presence stayed minimal for years while the app itself was the whole product.
Xbox.com launched alongside Microsoft's first console in 2001, marking the company's first serious entry into a gaming hardware market long dominated by Sony and Nintendo.
